new_candidates.body:
## Environment
* OS Version: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS (amd64)
* Source or binary build? Binary: `ros-humble-ros-gz-image` 0.244.26-1jammy.20260908, `libignition-transport11` 11.4.2, Gazebo Fortress 6.18.0, `ros-humble-image-transport` 3.1.13. The code involved is the same on the `humble` branch and, as far as we can tell, on `ros2`.

## Description
* Expected behavior: `image_bridge` exits cleanly on SIGINT.
* Actual behavior: it sometimes exits with SIGSEGV when a camera frame arrives during its teardown. We see it in about 1% of simulator shutdowns with a 30 Hz camera.

Cause, as far as we can tell, in [`ros_gz_image/src/image_bridge.cpp` at 0.244.26](https://github.com/gazebosim/ros_gz/blob/0.244.26/ros_gz_image/src/image_bridge.cpp):

- [line 42](https://github.com/gazebosim/ros_gz/blob/0.244.26/ros_gz_image/src/image_bridge.cpp#L42): `_gz_node->Subscribe(_topic, &Handler::OnImage, this);` binds the callback to a raw `this`.
- [lines 83 and 85](https://github.com/gazebosim/ros_gz/blob/0.244.26/ros_gz_image/src/image_bridge.cpp#L83-L85): `gz_node` is declared before `handlers`. When `rclcpp::spin()` returns after SIGINT, the `Handler`s, with their `image_transport::Publisher`s, are destroyed before the transport node.
- In ignition-transport 11, `NodeShared::RecvMsgUpdate` copies the handler list under its mutex, releases it, then runs the callbacks. So neither `~Node` nor `Unsubscribe` waits for a callback that is already running.

A frame received in that window calls `OnImage` on a destroyed `Handler` and faults in `image_transport::Publisher::publish`.

Reordering the two declarations alone would probably only narrow the window, since `~Node` doesn't wait for in-flight callbacks. What we tested is a guard in `Handler`: a mutex-protected `closed` flag, held while `OnImage` runs and set in the destructor, so `OnImage` returns at once after teardown starts. That removed the crash in the reproducer below (0 of 100 against 31 of 100).

Downstream we work around it by pausing the simulation before sending SIGINT to the bridge, so no frame is in flight.

## Steps to reproduce
A standalone reproducer with no Gazebo server: a Gazebo-transport image publisher plus the unmodified upstream `image_bridge` source, with the guard behind `-DGUARD_CALLBACK`. It's at [AIRclub-UdeSA/yahboom_rosmaster `yahboom_rosmaster_gazebo/tools/image_bridge_repro/`](https://github.com/AIRclub-UdeSA/yahboom_rosmaster/tree/c8bf23ef6e0adae9b4cac50a81cf1460127b2456/yahboom_rosmaster_gazebo/tools/image_bridge_repro).

1. `source /opt/ros/humble/setup.bash`, then `cmake -S yahboom_rosmaster_gazebo/tools/image_bridge_repro -B /tmp/ibr && cmake --build /tmp/ibr`
2. `python3 yahboom_rosmaster_gazebo/tools/image_bridge_repro/repro_driver.py --build /tmp/ibr --variant orig --rate 300 --trials 100 --out /tmp/ibr_orig.jsonl`. Each trial starts a fresh publisher (two 640x480 RGB topics) and bridge in their own transport partition, lets them connect, then sends the bridge SIGINT.
3. Count the trials that end in SIGSEGV.

Results, 100 trials each:

| Variant | SIGSEGV |
|---|---|
| upstream bridge, 300 Hz | 31/100 |
| upstream bridge, 30 Hz | 1/100 |
| upstream bridge, publisher stopped before SIGINT | 0/100 |
| bridge with the guard, 300 Hz | 0/100 |

## Output
Backtrace, the same in two crashes captured in the full simulator and in 6 of 8 crashes captured with the reproducer, taken by gdb from a fault handler. The faulting thread is the transport's reception thread:

```
RunReceptionTask -> NodeShared::RecvMsgUpdate -> TriggerCallbacks
  -> Handler::OnImage -> image_transport::Publisher::publish   (SIGSEGV, si_code 128)
```

The fault comes 5.4–5.6 ms after SIGINT, with the main thread already in `exit()` (static destructors), so `main()` has returned. The other 2 of 8 reproducer crashes faulted in `rcutils_logging_get_logger_effective_level`, called from the same `OnImage`.
new_candidates.title: image_bridge: segfault at shutdown when a frame arrives during teardown
